How a legendary UK comic ended up in a video game – Here’s The Dring
Plus, some words on GTA 6 and Gamescom, of course
Christopher Dring
Aug 31, 2026
∙ Paid
What should I write about GTA 6?
That’s the question I asked myself on my train home from Gamescom. Surely, I have to have a business opinion on the game’s epic Netflix reveal?
I did spend part of my Friday morning on various news channels (and one mainstream radio show) chatting about GTA 6, the Netflix reveal and the state of the video game industry. But… that was all stuff you know.
You know it’s been 13 years and the hype is at a level we’ve never experienced before. You know it’s going to break records. You know that the industry has had a brutal few years. And you know everyone is hoping Rockstar can single-handedly sort that out for us.
My one tiny observation is that in all of those mainstream media appearances I did, I was asked pretty good, reasonable questions. There was no eye-rolling. No fear-mongering. Finally, video games are being taken seriously!
Oh, wait, you knew that, too.
How about I talk about a beloved 67-year-old UK comedian turning up in a video game instead?
Yeah, let’s write about that.

How small UK indie Dlala secured Bob Mortimer for Murals
In Brief: Dlala Studios, the developer behind Disney Illusion Island and Battletoads, is working on a new IP called Murals. The action adventure game was announced during Gamescom Opening Night Live and features UK comic Bob Mortimer.
What You Need To Know:
Murals sees Dlala move away from licensed games and towards its own franchise. It features twisted reinterpretations of Hansel and Gretel, The Little Mermaid, Rapunzel, and more.
The 43-person development team is self-publishing the game. It hired former EA, Xbox and Unity exec Marcus Purvis as head of publishing, and is working with Tara Bruno PR.
Bob Mortimer is a UK national treasure, famous for TV shows such as Shooting Stars, Would I Lie To You, Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing and Last One Laughing.
Here’s The Dring
Ok, I will talk about Gamescom and GTA 6 in a moment. I promise.
But, when I saw that Bob Mortimer was going to star in a new indie game, I just had to find out about it.
To those not in the UK, Bob Mortimer is an absurdist and surrealist comedian that is much loved across the UK. He’s gentle, warm and very popular. He’s also not averse to a bit of gaming. In the last series of Amazon’s Last One Laughing, he briefly touched upon his love for the Resident Evil series.
I asked Dlala boss AJ Grand-Scrutton about how the partnership came about. And he went into such enthusiastic detail, I thought I just had to share it. So, here’s the story of how Bob Mortimer came to be in Murals.
“Kelsey Abbott, my lead writer, and I, were writing the game,” Grand-Scrutton told me. “We came to this character and we were like, ‘Let’s just rip off Bob Mortimer’. We love Bob Mortimer, let’s just make him talk like Bob Mortimer in our world. The character was even originally called Magic Bob.
“Then I was sitting at my desk and I thought… I’ve got to ask. If I ask, and get told no, that’s fine. So, I rung up Mark Landers at [audio company] Side. I said, ‘Hi Mark, it’s AJ.’ ‘Alright AJ, how’s it going?’ ‘You know how I ask these ridiculous and outrageous questions. Bob Mortimer… any chance?’ And he said, ‘Leave it with me’.
